ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows that one corner of a cube has already been cut off, forming an inward-concave three-faced notch. In this notch, 3 new internal square faces can be seen; the original top face and two side faces on the outside of the cube still belong to the original outer surface, only their shapes have had one corner dug out. Reasoning: The original 3×3×3 cube has 6 outer surfaces. Each time a 1×1×1 corner block is cut off, 3 internal square faces are added, without additionally splitting the original outer surface into new faces. A cube has 8 corners in total, so the total number of added faces is 8×3=24. The final total number of faces is 6+24=30.

method.method_draft: Use an incremental face-count argument. From the image, note that cutting one corner makes a trihedral notch: the three original outside side/top faces are not counted as new separate faces, while three new interior square faces appear inside the notch. From the text, the same operation is done at every corner of the original 3 by 3 by 3 cube. A cube starts with 6 faces, and it has 8 corners. Each corner cut adds 3 new faces, so the final count is 6 + 8*3 = 30.

method.method_draft: Classify the final surface into exterior and interior planar face regions. From the image, a corner cut creates three inward-facing square planar regions at one unit in from the original corner. From the text, this happens at all 8 corners of the 3 by 3 by 3 cube. First count the 6 original exterior side planes: after all four corners of a side are removed, each side remains one connected planar notched face. Then count the new interior faces: each of the 8 removed corner cubes contributes 3 exposed square faces, and these exposed faces are separated from those at other corners, so they do not merge. Thus the total is 6 exterior faces + 8*3 interior faces = 30.
